transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I'm honestly only here because my RA and campus health were worried about my weight and mentioned medical leave, which terrified me because I don't want to lose my academic progress. I just feel like if I don’t keep really tight control over what I eat, I’ll gain weight and everything I’ve worked so hard for will fall apart.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'tight control' over your eating, and how your fears about gaining weight affect your daily food choices and overall behavior?

I keep a strict calorie-tracking spreadsheet on my laptop and mostly just have black coffee in the morning, half a granola bar between classes, and a tiny salad at night. If I even think about eating normal college food like pizza or ice cream, I panic, so I've started skipping club meetings and turning down group dinners to avoid messing up my schedule.
Do you often check your body weight, and if so, how frequently do you weigh yourself, as this might help us understand your concerns better?

Yes, I weigh myself every morning, and that number completely dictates my entire mood and sense of worth for the day. If the scale is lower, I feel like I'm finally doing something right and deserve to be in the honors program and become an art therapist. But if it goes up by even half a pound, I feel disgusting and completely unworthy of any of my roles on campus.
Have you experienced any changes in your menstrual cycle, such as irregular periods or a complete stop, since you started tightly controlling your eating and exercising?
I haven't really been paying much attention to that, to be honest. I've been so stressed with my classes and my art portfolio that I'm not really sure if my periods have changed or not.

Let's take a closer look at your menstrual cycle; can you try to recall the last time you had a period, and if you've noticed any changes in how often you get your period since you started your strict diet and exercise regimen?

I honestly can't recall the last time I had it, and I'm not sure if the timing has changed. I've just been so completely focused on my classes and keeping up with my daily routine that I haven't paid any attention to it.
Can you try to think back to the last time you had a period, or at least estimate how long it's been since your last period, as this information is important for understanding your overall health?

I honestly can't even guess because I haven't kept track of it at all. My mind has been completely consumed by my studio art critiques and keeping up my grades, so I'm really not sure when it last happened. It's just not something I've been paying attention to.
Have you had any menstrual period in the past three months, as this will help clarify the impact of your eating habits on your reproductive health?
I'm really not sure, because I haven't been keeping track of it at all lately. I've been so overwhelmed with my studio art projects and academic stress that I just haven't paid any attention to it.

To clarify, you're unsure if you've had a menstrual period in the past three months, but can you confirm if you've had any periods at all in the past year, as this will help us understand the potential effects of your diet and stress on your menstrual cycle?

I'm really not sure about the exact timing of my periods over the past year because I haven't paid close attention to it. I've been so completely focused on my classes and keeping up with my daily food routines that it just wasn't on my radar.
Have you had any menstrual periods at all in the past year, as this information is crucial for understanding the potential impact of your eating habits and stress on your reproductive health?

I'm really not sure, and I don't want to guess and give you the wrong information. I've just been so completely focused on my classes and keeping up with my daily routines that I haven't paid any attention to it at all this past year.
To confirm, you're saying you can't recall having a menstrual period in the past year, is that correct?
Yes, that's correct. I honestly just haven't kept track of it at all, so I really can't say for sure one way or the other.
Can you confirm if you have noticed any other physical symptoms such as hair loss, cold intolerance, or fatigue, which might be related to your eating habits and potential hormonal changes?

I do get really cold in class sometimes and feel tired or lightheaded, but I haven't noticed any hair loss. Honestly, I don't think it's a major medical issue or that I'm sick enough for it to be serious, since I'm still walking to all my classes and keeping my grades up.

Can you describe how often you feel tired or lightheaded, and if these feelings are related to your meals or activities, as this might help us understand how your eating habits are affecting your overall health?

I usually feel dizzy or tired between my classes or when I'm working for hours in the art studio, and I'll sometimes eat half a granola bar if I feel faint just to keep going. But I really don't think it's serious enough to warrant medical leave like they said. I'm still pushing through every day and keeping my grades up, so it's not like I'm too sick to be here.

You mentioned you can't recall having a menstrual period in the past year, can you confirm if you've experienced any other symptoms like breast tenderness, mood swings, or any vaginal discharge, which could help us better understand your condition?

I haven't really noticed any of those symptoms, and I'm not sure about mood swings because I'm just generally stressed about my classes. Honestly, the only physical things I've really felt are just being constantly cold and tired.

Can you estimate your current weight and tell me what you believe would be a 'healthy' or 'acceptable' weight for yourself, as this might help us understand your motivations and fears around eating and weight gain?

I'm not really sure of the exact numbers right now, and I don't really want to focus on a specific weight. I just feel like my current weight is still too high, and I need to keep losing more before I can feel safe and in control.
Do you believe that your weight and body shape are directly tied to your self-worth and identity as a student and future art therapist?

Yes, they absolutely are. When the scale is lower, I feel like I'm finally doing something right and that I'm actually worthy of being in the honors program and becoming an art therapist. But if it goes up even half a pound, I feel disgusting and like I don't deserve to be in any of my roles on campus.

Can you confirm if you have experienced any amenorrhea, or the absence of menstruation, for more than three months, as this can help differentiate between anorexia nervosa and other potential diagnoses?
I'm really not sure, to be honest. Like I've mentioned, I just haven't paid close attention to my menstrual cycle recently because I've been so overwhelmed with my schoolwork and daily routines.
